questions.text: Regarding the transformation of Bharatanatyam from Sadir to its modern form, which of the following statements accurately describes the role of Rukmini Devi Arundale?

options.text: She exclusively preserved the hereditary Devadasi repertoire without any modifications to technique or costume.

questions.text: In the structural anatomy of a Carnatic Kriti, which of the following correctly identifies the typical characteristics of the Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Charanam sections?

options.label: A
options.text: The Pallavi is the longest and concluding section; the Anupallavi is the opening thematic statement; the Charanam is the middle section.

options.text: The Pallavi and Anupallavi are improvisational sections (Manodharma), while the Charanam is the only pre-composed section.

options.text: The Charanam serves as the opening refrain; the Pallavi contains the composer's mudra (signature); the Anupallavi is the longest section.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the Indian People's Theatre Association (IPTA) and its approach to theatre forms?

questions.text: The Indo-Gangetic Plain is divided into three sub-regions based on the river systems that feed them. Which sub-region is characterised by a braided channel network and frequent avulsions?

questions.text: Regarding the Peninsular Plateau, which statement accurately reflects the geological features of the Deccan Traps and the Western Ghats?

options.text: He retained the jarib of 60 gaz as the primary measuring rod for all surveys.

options.label: D
options.text: He delegated measurement standards to hereditary qanungos without central oversight.

questions.solution: Correct answer: He introduced a uniform bigha of 3,025 square yards, replacing heterogeneous local units..

questions.text: Regarding the Mughal dahsala system under Akbar, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It mandated an annual reassessment of land revenue based on current harvest yields.

options.label: B
options.text: It fixed the state demand at one-half of the estimated produce for all crop categories.

options.label: C
options.text: It used a decennial (ten-year) average of actual yields to smooth seasonal fluctuations.

options.label: D
options.text: It applied uniformly to all provinces including the Deccan subahs from 1580 onwards.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It used a decennial (ten-year) average of actual yields to smooth seasonal fluctuations..

questions.text: The origin of the double-dome technique in Indo-Islamic architecture is correctly attributed to:

options.label: A
options.text: Mughal architects under Humayun, first seen in his tomb at Delhi.

options.label: B
options.text: Lodi period tombs, later refined by Mughal architects.

options.label: C
options.text: Persian master builders imported during Akbar's reign.

options.label: D
options.text: The Suri dynasty, as evidenced by Sher Shah's tomb at Sasaram.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Lodi period tombs, later refined by Mughal architects..

questions.text: Which statement best reflects the operational reality of the Portuguese cartaz system in Mughal India?

options.label: A
options.text: It was uniformly enforced on all Asian shipping without exception.

options.label: B
options.text: Mughal vessels frequently obtained exemptions through imperial farmans.

options.label: C
options.text: It applied only to European ships entering Portuguese-controlled ports.

options.label: D
options.text: It was abolished by Akbar's firman of 1573 granting free trade to all.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Mughal vessels frequently obtained exemptions through imperial farmans..

questions.text: The fundamental distinction between the Maratha 'sea-chauth' and the land 'chauth' was that the sea-chauth:

options.label: A
options.text: Was a 25% protective tribute levied on agrarian revenue in coastal districts.

options.label: B
options.text: Functioned as a customs duty on shipping entering the Konkan littoral.

options.label: C
options.text: Was collected by the Portuguese on behalf of the Angres under treaty.

options.label: D
options.text: Applied only to European vessels and exempted Indian merchantmen.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Functioned as a customs duty on shipping entering the Konkan littoral..

questions.text: What was the principal fiscal innovation of Jahangir's du-aspah sih-aspah mansab classification introduced around 1620?

options.label: A
options.text: It allowed the sawar (cavalry) rank to exceed the zat (personal) rank without a proportional increase in salary.

options.label: B
options.text: It merged the zat and sawar ranks into a single unified rank to simplify payroll.

options.label: C
options.text: It reduced the zat rank of all mansabdars by half to cut treasury expenditure.

options.label: D
options.text: It mandated that jagir revenue assignments be paid in cash rather than land grants.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It allowed the sawar (cavalry) rank to exceed the zat (personal) rank without a proportional increase in salary..

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the integrative function of the Mahanayakacharya in the Vijayanagara Empire?

options.label: A
options.text: He served solely as the commander-in-chief of the imperial army during wartime.

options.label: B
options.text: He coordinated nayaka appointments, temple revenues, irrigation works, and trade mediation to align provincial power with central policy.

options.label: C
options.text: He functioned as the chief priest of the Virupaksha temple, legitimizing royal authority through ritual.

options.label: D
options.text: He was the empire's chief revenue auditor, responsible only for assessing land tax yields.

questions.solution: Correct answer: He coordinated nayaka appointments, temple revenues, irrigation works, and trade mediation to align provincial power with central policy..

questions.text: The Ahom paik system is most accurately characterized as:

options.label: A
options.text: A land revenue tax collected in kind from peasant cultivators.

options.label: B
options.text: A corvée labour obligation tied to hereditary land grants (gaonburha) and mandatory military service.

options.label: C
options.text: A mercenary recruitment system where soldiers were paid fixed salaries from the royal treasury.

options.label: D
options.text: A guild-based craft production quota imposed on artisan communities.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A corvée labour obligation tied to hereditary land grants (gaonburha) and mandatory military service..

questions.text: Regarding Maratha revenue administration, which statement correctly distinguishes the kamavisdar from the Mughal faujdar?

options.label: A
options.text: The kamavisdar was a military governor with judicial powers, while the faujdar was a pure revenue collector.

options.label: B
options.text: The kamavisdar operated on a salary-plus-commission basis as a revenue officer, whereas the faujdar was primarily a military-administrative governor.

options.label: C
options.text: The kamavisdar held hereditary and non-revocable tenure, unlike the transferable faujdar.

options.label: D
options.text: The kamavisdar reported directly to the Peshwa's household, while the faujdar reported to the provincial diwan.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The kamavisdar operated on a salary-plus-commission basis as a revenue officer, whereas the faujdar was primarily a military-administrative governor..

questions.text: The resilience of Deccan Sultanate forts during prolonged sieges (e.g., Bijapur 1565, Golconda 1686) depended critically on:

options.label: A
options.text: The adoption of European trace italienne bastion geometry after 1500.

options.label: B
options.text: Subterranean karez channels feeding internal cisterns (hauz) that secured water and logistical endurance.

options.label: C
options.text: The exclusive use of heavy bronze cannon mounted on curtain walls for offensive bombardment.

options.label: D
options.text: Diplomatic alliances with European trading companies for ammunition resupply by sea.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Subterranean karez channels feeding internal cisterns (hauz) that secured water and logistical endurance..

questions.text: Regarding the monetary reforms from the Khaljis to the Mughals, which statement is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: Alauddin Khalji's token-currency experiment failed due to widespread counterfeiting, forcing a return to silver.

options.label: B
options.text: Sher Shah Suri standardized the silver rupee at 11.66 g and established a bimetallic ratio of 1 rupee = 40 dams.

options.label: C
options.text: Muhammad bin Tughluq's brass and copper tokens were introduced as a weight standard similar to Sher Shah's rupee.

options.label: D
options.text: Aurangzeb's Deccan wars led to an increase in silver inflow from Portuguese trade at Surat.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Sher Shah Suri standardized the silver rupee at 11.66 g and established a bimetallic ratio of 1 rupee = 40 dams..

questions.text: In the Mughal provincial administration, which of the following pairs correctly matches the official with their function and territorial level?

options.label: A
options.text: Subahdar – Sole revenue authority at the Subah level.

options.label: B
options.text: Faujdar – Police function at the Pargana level.

options.label: C
options.text: Shiqdar – Military role at the Sarkar level.

options.label: D
options.text: Diwan – Joint fiscal control with central audit (hasil) at the Subah level.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Diwan – Joint fiscal control with central audit (hasil) at the Subah level..

questions.text: The 'jagirdari crisis' of the late Mughal period is best characterized by which of the following structural mismatches?

options.label: A
options.text: An absolute shortage of cultivable land relative to the number of mansabdars.

options.label: B
options.text: A mismatch between the number of mansabdars, their sawar obligations, and actual revenue yield.

options.label: C
options.text: The refusal of mansabdars to maintain stipulated troop contingents due to religious dissent.

options.label: D
options.text: The transfer of all revenue-farming rights (ijara) to the peasantry, bypassing moneylenders.

questions.solution: Correct answer: A mismatch between the number of mansabdars, their sawar obligations, and actual revenue yield..

questions.text: Which statement accurately reflects the dynamics of literary patronage under the Sultanate and Mughals?

options.label: A
options.text: Persian completely displaced regional languages as the sole medium of courtly and devotional literature.

options.label: B
options.text: The translation of the Mahabharata into Persian as the Razmnama was commissioned by the Bahmani court in the Deccan.

options.label: C
options.text: The Mughal practice of granting madad-i-ma'ash to scholars irrespective of language encouraged a multilingual literary ecosystem.

options.label: D
options.text: Dakhni Urdu literature, such as the Qissa-i-Yusuf, flourished under the patronage of the Yadava and Maratha courts in the Deccan.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Mughal practice of granting madad-i-ma'ash to scholars irrespective of language encouraged a multilingual literary ecosystem..

questions.text: What was the primary change in revenue assessment after the Mughal annexation of the Gujarat Sultanate in 1573?

options.label: A
options.text: Continuation of the Sultanate's kharaj based on cultivated area

options.label: B
options.text: Adoption of the Mughal zabt system with standardized measurement (bigha) and the dahsala ten‑year average

options.label: C
options.text: Introduction of new iqta assignments for local nobles

options.label: D
options.text: Abolition of all land revenue in favour of trade taxes

questions.solution: Correct answer: Adoption of the Mughal zabt system with standardized measurement (bigha) and the dahsala ten‑year average.

questions.text: Which statement accurately describes the production of Maratha artillery such as zamzama and farangi guns in the 17th century?

options.label: A
options.text: They were entirely imported from European foundries

options.label: B
options.text: They were produced mainly in indigenous foundries at Pune and Satara

options.label: C
options.text: They were only captured from Mughal arsenals

options.label: D
options.text: They were manufactured exclusively by Portuguese craftsmen

questions.solution: Correct answer: They were produced mainly in indigenous foundries at Pune and Satara.

questions.text: How did Vijayanagara temple grants function beyond religious endowments?

options.label: A
options.text: They were purely religious with no fiscal duties

options.label: B
options.text: They carried explicit fiscal obligations and were subject to state audit mechanisms

options.label: C
options.text: They were limited to land grants for Brahmin priests only

options.label: D
options.text: They were managed solely by merchant guilds without state oversight

questions.solution: Correct answer: They carried explicit fiscal obligations and were subject to state audit mechanisms.

questions.text: What was the nature of Portuguese cartazes in the Deccan region during 1500‑1650?

options.label: A
options.text: Voluntary trade licences that merchants could accept or decline

options.label: B
options.text: Enforced by naval patrols; non‑compliance led to seizure of vessels

options.label: C
options.text: Issued only to Mughal imperial ships

options.label: D
options.text: Replaced by Mughal permits after 1600

questions.solution: Correct answer: Enforced by naval patrols; non‑compliance led to seizure of vessels.

questions.text: What role did the hereditary qanungo play in the Mughal zabt system's revenue assessment?

options.label: C
options.text: Reported directly to the emperor, bypassing local officials

questions.solution: Correct answer: His hereditary tenure aligned his interests with the zamindar, leading to collusive under‑reporting.

questions.text: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between the British East India Company and

questions.text: Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935: 1. It provided for provincial autonomy. 2. It established a Federal Court. 3. It abolished separate electorates. 4. It introduced dyarchy at the centre. Which of the statements given above are correct?

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately distinguishes the Permanent Settlement of Bengal from the Ryotwari system?

options.text: The Permanent Settlement was devised by Thomas Munro, while Ryotwari was devised by Lord Cornwallis

questions.text: The "drain of wealth" theory articulated by early Indian nationalists primarily referred to:

questions.text: The Satyashodhak Samaj founded by Jyotirao Phule in 1873 differed from the Brahmo Samaj and Prarthana Samaj primarily in its:

questions.text: Which Charter Act introduced competitive examination for entry into the covenanted civil service and separated the executive and legislative functions of the Governor‑General's council?

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the origin and nature of the first Famine Codes in British India?

questions.text: Consider the following political associations: (1) British Indian Association, (2) Indian Association, (3) Poona Sarvajanik Sabha, (4) National Conference. Which sequence correctly orders them by year of foundation?

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the post-1857 reorganisation of the Indian Army is correct?

questions.text: With reference to the "guarantee system" for railway construction in India (1849-1869), which statement is accurate?

options.text: The IMS was fully Indianised by 1885 following the 1857 Revolt

options.label: C
options.text: Indian physicians were appointed as Surgeon‑Generals from 1862 onward

options.label: D
options.text: The IMS was merged with the Indian Civil Service in 1870

questions.solution: Correct answer: Senior posts in the IMS remained reserved for British officers throughout this period.

questions.text: The rapid expansion of the Bombay cotton textile industry between 1854 and 1885 was primarily catalysed by which external event?

options.label: A
options.text: The American Civil War (1861‑65) which disrupted Confederate cotton supplies to Lancashire

options.label: B
options.text: The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 reducing freight costs

options.label: C
options.text: The Indian Tariff Act of 1879 imposing a 5 % duty on British yarn

options.label: D
options.text: The establishment of the Managing Agency system by European firms

questions.solution: Correct answer: The American Civil War (1861‑65) which disrupted Confederate cotton supplies to Lancashire.

questions.text: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Indian Forest Act of 1865 from the Forest Act of 1878?

options.label: A
options.text: The 1865 Act classified forests into Reserved, Protected, and Village categories, while the 1878 Act merely empowered the government to declare government forests.

options.label: B
options.text: The 1865 Act was a declaratory statute empowering the government to declare government forests, while the 1878 Act introduced the three-fold classification of forests.

options.label: C
options.text: The 1865 Act established the Dehra Dun Forest School for professional training, while the 1878 Act focused solely on revenue extraction from timber.

options.label: D
options.text: The 1865 Act extinguished all customary rights of tribal communities, while the 1878 Act recorded and protected existing rights in Protected Forests.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The 1865 Act was a declaratory statute empowering the government to declare government forests, while the 1878 Act introduced the three-fold classification of forests..

questions.text: Which method characterises the Moderate phase (1885‑1905) of the Indian National Congress?

options.label: A
options.text: Boycott of British goods and promotion of Swadeshi

options.label: B
options.text: Prayer and petition: delegations to London, memoranda to the Secretary of State, and resolutions at annual sessions

options.label: C
options.text: Armed revolutionary activity and secret societies

options.label: D
options.text: Mass civil disobedience and non‑cooperation

questions.solution: Correct answer: Prayer and petition: delegations to London, memoranda to the Secretary of State, and resolutions at annual sessions.

questions.text: What ideological influences shaped the Extremist critique of British rule (1905‑1910)?

options.label: A
options.text: Faith in British constitutionalism and gradual reform

options.label: B
options.text: Writings of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, Swami Vivekananda, and the Irish nationalist experience

options.label: C
options.text: Theosophical teachings of Annie Besant and the demand for dominion status

options.label: D
options.text: Acceptance of the Morley‑Minto Reforms as a sufficient step toward self‑government

questions.solution: Correct answer: Writings of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, Swami Vivekananda, and the Irish nationalist experience.

questions.text: Which feature distinguishes the Home Rule Movement (1915‑1918) from the earlier Moderate and Extremist phases?

options.label: A
options.text: Demand for complete independence (Purna Swaraj) through revolutionary violence

options.label: B
options.text: Organisation of mass enrolment leagues, public lectures, and petition drives demanding dominion status within the Empire

options.label: C
options.text: Reliance solely on petitions to the British Parliament without any public mobilisation

options.label: D
options.text: Introduction of separate electorates for Muslims through the Morley‑Minto Reforms

questions.solution: Correct answer: Organisation of mass enrolment leagues, public lectures, and petition drives demanding dominion status within the Empire.

questions.text: The Rowlatt Committee (1918) recommended the continuation of which powers in peacetime, leading to the Rowlatt Act 1919?

options.label: A
options.text: Powers under the Defence of India Act 1915

options.label: B
options.text: Powers under the Indian Press Act 1910

options.label: C
options.text: Powers under the Newspaper (Incitement to Offences) Act 1908

options.label: D
options.text: Powers under the Rowlatt Act 1919 itself

questions.solution: Correct answer: Powers under the Defence of India Act 1915.

questions.text: Which of the following accurately describes a key political consequence of the 1911 reversal of the Partition of Bengal, as distinct from the 1905 partition itself?

options.label: A
options.text: It led to the immediate grant of separate electorates for Muslims through the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.

options.label: B
options.text: The creation of Bihar and Orissa as a separate province altered the demographic balance in the Bengal legislative council, strengthening the Muslim League's platform for separate electorates.

options.label: C
options.text: The capital shift from Calcutta to Delhi was primarily intended to appease the Bengali intelligentsia and reduce revolutionary violence.

options.label: D
options.text: Moderates and Extremists within the Indian National Congress unanimously welcomed the annulment as a victory for constitutional agitation.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The creation of Bihar and Orissa as a separate province altered the demographic balance in the Bengal legislative council, strengthening the Muslim League's platform for separate electorates..

questions.text: Regarding the Ghadar Party and the Home Rule Movement, which statement correctly identifies a fundamental difference in their objectives and methods?

options.label: A
options.text: Both movements sought dominion status through constitutional pressure within the British Empire.

options.label: B
options.text: The Ghadar Party aimed for complete independence through armed revolt leveraging the First World War, while the Home Rule Leagues demanded dominion status through constitutional pressure.

options.label: C
options.text: The Home Rule Movement was a transnational network founded by Indian expatriates in North America, whereas the Ghadar Party operated primarily within India.

options.label: D
options.text: The Ghadar Party's newspaper 'Ghadar' was published openly in Calcutta, while the Home Rule League's 'New India' circulated clandestinely aboard ships.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Ghadar Party aimed for complete independence through armed revolt leveraging the First World War, while the Home Rule Leagues demanded dominion status through constitutional pressure..

questions.text: The Indian Press Act of 1910 selectively suppressed nationalist newspapers primarily through which financial mechanism?

options.label: A
options.text: Imposition of heavy customs duties on imported newsprint and printing machinery.

options.label: B
options.text: Mandatory security deposits that could be forfeited for 'seditious' content, disproportionately affecting low-circulation revolutionary papers.

options.label: C
options.text: A progressive tax on newspaper circulation revenue that targeted high-readership moderate journals.

options.label: D
options.text: Licensing fees scaled to the political affiliation of the editor, with higher fees for known extremists.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Mandatory security deposits that could be forfeited for 'seditious' content, disproportionately affecting low-circulation revolutionary papers..

questions.text: How did the Montagu Declaration of 1917 differ from a firm promise of immediate dominion status, and how did key nationalist factions respond?

options.label: A
options.text: It committed to 'progressive realisation' of responsible government without a timetable; Moderates welcomed it, Extremists rejected it as inadequate, and Home Rule leaders demanded clearer guarantees.

options.label: B
options.text: It promised immediate dominion status after the war; all factions united in support, leading to the 1919 Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.

options.label: C
options.text: It offered only provincial autonomy with no central responsibility; Moderates opposed it, while Extremists and Home Rule leaders accepted it as a first step.

options.label: D
options.text: It declared full independence as the ultimate goal with a fixed 1920 deadline; the British retracted it under pressure from the Ghadar Party.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It committed to 'progressive realisation' of responsible government without a timetable; Moderates welcomed it, Extremists rejected it as inadequate, and Home Rule leaders demanded clearer guarantees..

questions.text: Which of the following represents an unprecedented formal organisational role for women in the Home Rule Movement (1916-1918), as distinct from their participation in the earlier Swadeshi Movement?

options.label: A
options.text: Women served as 'district organisers' in Annie Besant's Home Rule League, a formal title with defined responsibilities like coordinating lecture tours and managing vernacular pamphlet distribution.

options.label: B
options.text: Women participated in picketing foreign cloth shops and burning imported goods, activities that began during Swadeshi and continued unchanged into Home Rule.

options.label: C
options.text: Women were elected as presidents of provincial Home Rule League branches, exercising authority over male members.

options.label: D
options.text: Women's involvement was limited to fundraising and attending meetings, with no formal organisational positions in either movement.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Women served as 'district organisers' in Annie Besant's Home Rule League, a formal title with defined responsibilities like coordinating lecture tours and managing vernacular pamphlet distribution..

questions.text: The 1905 Russo-Japanese War influenced Extremist strategic thinking in India primarily by:

options.label: A
options.text: Providing a model for constitutional petitioning within the British imperial framework

options.label: B
options.text: Demonstrating that an Asian power could defeat a European power through modernisation and national spirit

options.label: C
options.text: Encouraging the Moderates to accelerate negotiations for the Morley-Minto Reforms

options.label: D
options.text: Leading to the immediate formation of the Ghadar Party in Punjab

questions.solution: Correct answer: Demonstrating that an Asian power could defeat a European power through modernisation and national spirit.

questions.text: The 1916 Lucknow Pact's provision for Muslim weightage in legislative councils was:

options.label: A
options.text: A permanent constitutional guarantee that could not be altered without Muslim League consent

options.label: B
options.text: Superseded by the 1919 Government of India Act and later negotiations

options.label: C
options.text: Rejected by the Congress at the 1917 Home Rule Conference

options.label: D
options.text: Extended to all minorities including Sikhs and Christians in the same session

questions.solution: Correct answer: Superseded by the 1919 Government of India Act and later negotiations.

questions.text: The fundamental difference between the Home Rule Movement's demand (1916-1918) and the later 'Purna Swaraj' resolution (1929) was that the former:

options.label: A
options.text: Demanded complete severance from the British Crown

options.label: B
options.text: Accepted Crown suzerainty in external affairs while seeking full internal autonomy

options.label: C
options.text: Was based on the American republican model rather than the British dominion model

options.label: D
options.text: Explicitly rejected the Montagu Declaration's promise of responsible government

questions.solution: Correct answer: Accepted Crown suzerainty in external affairs while seeking full internal autonomy.

questions.text: What was the specific constitutional commitment made by the British Government in the Montagu Declaration of 1917?

options.label: A
options.text: Immediate grant of Home Rule (self-government) to India on par with the Dominions.

options.label: B
options.text: Progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the British Empire.

options.label: C
options.text: Establishment of a fully elected legislative assembly with control over the executive (Swaraj).

options.label: D
options.text: Implementation of the Lucknow Pact provisions regarding separate electorates and provincial autonomy.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the British Empire..

questions.text: Which legislative measure enacted in 1910 mandated publishers to deposit security with the government, liable to forfeiture for publishing seditious material, leading to the closure of many nationalist newspapers?

options.label: A
options.text: Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act, 1908

options.label: B
options.text: Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1908

options.label: C
options.text: Press Act, 1910

options.label: D
options.text: Defence of India Act, 1915

questions.solution: Correct answer: Press Act, 1910.

questions.text: Which of the following provisions was introduced for the first time by the Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley‑Minto Reforms)?

options.label: A
options.text: Separate electorates for Muslims

options.label: B
options.text: Indians gaining control over the provincial budget

options.label: C
options.text: Abolition of the Viceroy's executive council

options.label: D
options.text: Extension of separate electorates to Sikhs and Christians

questions.solution: Correct answer: Separate electorates for Muslims.

questions.text: Which medium was primarily responsible for disseminating symbolic icons such as Bharat Mata to the masses during the Extremist phase?

options.label: A
options.text: English‑language newspapers reaching the urban elite

options.label: B
options.text: Vernacular presses in Bengali, Marathi, Tamil and other languages

options.label: C
options.text: Official government gazettes

options.label: D
options.text: International socialist journals

questions.solution: Correct answer: Vernacular presses in Bengali, Marathi, Tamil and other languages.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the role of the Indian Civil Service (ICS) in the enforcement of the 1910 Press Act?

options.label: A
options.text: ICS officers were exclusively British and uniformly enforced the Act without dissent.

options.label: B
options.text: District Magistrates, who were ICS officers, could order seizure of presses and detain editors without trial.

options.label: C
options.text: The Act was enforced by the newly created Intelligence Branch, bypassing the district administration.

options.label: D
options.text: Sir Henry Cotton, as an ICS officer, used his position to strengthen the implementation of the Act.

questions.solution: Correct answer: District Magistrates, who were ICS officers, could order seizure of presses and detain editors without trial..

questions.text: Under the Defence of India Act 1915, which section authorised the establishment of special tribunals that could try offences in camera and award sentences up to transportation for life?

options.label: A
options.text: Section 10

options.label: B
options.text: Section 12

options.label: C
options.text: Section 13

options.label: D
options.text: Section 14

questions.solution: Correct answer: Section 12.

questions.text: The 1917 August Declaration by Edwin Montagu marked a significant policy shift by redefining the goal of British policy in India. What was the new stated goal that replaced the demand for Home Rule?

options.label: A
options.text: Dominion Status

options.label: B
options.text: Responsible Government

options.label: C
options.text: Provincial Autonomy

options.label: D
options.text: Complete Independence

questions.solution: Correct answer: Responsible Government.

questions.text: Which indigenous financial institution failed in 1914 due to the 1913‑14 recession triggered by a fall in jute prices, as mentioned in the text?

options.label: A
options.text: Punjab National Bank

options.label: B
options.text: Bengal National Bank

options.label: C
options.text: Bank of India

options.label: D
options.text: Central Bank of India

questions.solution: Correct answer: Bengal National Bank.

questions.text: Which of the following accurately describes the principal reason the Rowlatt Act of 1919 provoked nationwide opposition?

options.label: A
options.text: It was passed with the unanimous support of Indian members of the Imperial Legislative Council.

options.label: B
options.text: It extended wartime emergency powers into peacetime, allowing detention without trial and restricting civil liberties.

options.label: C
options.text: It was a direct response to the Non‑Cooperation Movement launched by Gandhi in 1920.

options.label: D
options.text: It granted full civil liberties and abolished preventive detention.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It extended wartime emergency powers into peacetime, allowing detention without trial and restricting civil liberties..

questions.text: What was Gandhi's immediate response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre on 13 April 1919?

options.label: A
options.text: He intensified the Rowlatt Satyagraha and called for a nationwide strike.

options.label: B
options.text: He suspended the satyagraha on 18 April 1919, arguing the movement had lost its non‑violent character.

options.label: C
options.text: He demanded the immediate repeal of the Rowlatt Act and the prosecution of General Dyer.

options.label: D
options.text: He announced the launch of the Non‑Cooperation Movement at the Nagpur session.

questions.solution: Correct answer: He suspended the satyagraha on 18 April 1919, arguing the movement had lost its non‑violent character..

questions.text: Which woman is credited with operating an underground radio station during the Quit India Movement (1942)?

options.label: A
options.text: Sarojini Naidu

options.label: B
options.text: Usha Mehta

options.label: C
options.text: Kasturba Gandhi

options.label: D
options.text: Rani Gaidinliu

questions.solution: Correct answer: Usha Mehta.

questions.text: In which year was the All India Kisan Sabha founded and who was its first president?

options.label: A
options.text: 1934, N. G. Ranga

options.label: B
options.text: 1936, Swami Sahajanand Saraswati

options.label: C
options.text: 1939, Indulal Yagnik

options.label: D
options.text: 1942, Communist Party of India

questions.solution: Correct answer: 1936, Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.

questions.text: What was the primary factor that galvanised Indian public opinion in favour of the Indian National Army (INA)?

options.label: A
options.text: Military victories of the INA in Burma

options.label: B
options.text: The Red Fort Trials of INA officers

options.label: C
options.text: Subhas Chandra Bose's radio broadcasts from Southeast Asia

options.label: D
options.text: The formation of the Azad Hind Government in Singapore

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Red Fort Trials of INA officers.

questions.text: The Poona Pact (1932) replaced the separate electorates for the Depressed Classes, as provided in the Communal Award, with which arrangement?

options.label: A
options.text: Separate electorates for Muslims only

options.label: B
options.text: Reserved seats in joint electorates

options.label: C
options.text: Universal adult franchise for all communities

options.label: D
options.text: A weighted voting system favouring landlords

questions.solution: Correct answer: Reserved seats in joint electorates.

questions.text: Which feature was introduced by the Government of India Act 1935 but was absent in the 1919 Act?

options.label: A
options.text: Dyarchy at the provincial level

options.label: B
options.text: Full provincial autonomy with all subjects transferred

options.label: C
options.text: Limited franchise based on property qualifications

options.label: D
options.text: Separate electorates for Muslims only

questions.solution: Correct answer: Full provincial autonomy with all subjects transferred.

questions.text: Which of the following was NOT a measure undertaken by the Congress ministries formed in 1937?

options.label: A
options.text: Release of political prisoners

options.label: B
options.text: Introduction of tenancy legislation to protect peasants

options.label: C
options.text: Nationalisation of railways

options.label: D
options.text: Promotion of khadi and village industries

questions.solution: Correct answer: Nationalisation of railways.

questions.text: What was the immediate trigger for the Royal Indian Navy mutiny in February 1946?

options.label: A
options.text: Demand for higher pay and better pensions

options.label: B
options.text: Racial discrimination, poor food, and the arrest of a rating for writing a slogan

options.label: C
options.text: Refusal to obey orders to sail to Southeast Asia

options.label: D
options.text: Political demand for immediate independence

questions.solution: Correct answer: Racial discrimination, poor food, and the arrest of a rating for writing a slogan.

questions.text: Which organisational step did Jinnah take after the 1937 elections to expand the Muslim League’s mass base?

options.label: A
options.text: Launching a new English‑language newspaper

options.label: B
options.text: Appointing provincial organising secretaries and opening district‑level offices

options.label: C
options.text: Forming a coalition government with the Congress in United Provinces

options.label: D
options.text: Requesting the British to increase Muslim representation in the civil services

questions.solution: Correct answer: Appointing provincial organising secretaries and opening district‑level offices.

questions.text: Which of the following statements accurately describes the British censorship regime against the vernacular press between 1919 and 1947?

options.label: A
options.text: The Indian Press Act of 1910 was repealed after the Non-Cooperation Movement and replaced by a single comprehensive Defence of India Rules.

options.label: B
options.text: The Indian Press (Emergency Powers) Act of 1931 empowered district magistrates to demand security deposits, seize presses, and imprison editors.

options.label: C
options.text: During the Quit India Movement, the British permitted Congress-affiliated papers to operate under strict guidelines to monitor nationalist sentiment.

options.label: D
options.text: The Defence of India Rules were invoked only during the 1942 Quit India phase and not during World War II's earlier years.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Indian Press (Emergency Powers) Act of 1931 empowered district magistrates to demand security deposits, seize presses, and imprison editors..

questions.text: Regarding the 1943 Bengal Famine, which factor was a deliberate wartime policy choice by the colonial administration rather than a natural calamity?

options.label: A
options.text: The severe cyclone in October 1942 that destroyed the aman harvest.

options.label: B
options.text: The Japanese occupation of Burma cutting off rice imports.

options.label: C
options.text: The 'denial policy' involving destruction of boats and stockpiles to prevent Japanese use.

options.label: D
options.text: The global shipping shortage caused by Allied military requirements.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The 'denial policy' involving destruction of boats and stockpiles to prevent Japanese use..

questions.text: The integration of princely states into the Indian Union (1945-1948) involved which combination of methods?

options.label: A
options.text: Exclusively diplomatic negotiations and standstill agreements without any military intervention.

options.label: B
options.text: Military action in Hyderabad, plebiscites in Junagadh and Kashmir, and popular uprisings in Travancore.

options.label: C
options.text: A uniform process of referendums supervised by the United Nations across all princely states.

options.label: D
options.text: Voluntary accession by all rulers following the lapse of paramountcy, with no resistance encountered.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Military action in Hyderabad, plebiscites in Junagadh and Kashmir, and popular uprisings in Travancore..

questions.text: The INA Trials (1945-46) significantly eroded British authority primarily because:

options.label: A
options.text: The courts-martial strictly followed legal procedures and convicted all defendants, demonstrating British judicial fairness.

options.label: B
options.text: The trials functioned as political theatre that mobilised both civilians and serving soldiers, triggering the RIN mutiny and mass protests.

options.label: C
options.text: The Congress and Muslim League boycotted the trials, denying them political legitimacy and forcing British withdrawal.

options.label: D
options.text: The British government immediately pardoned all INA officers after the first trial to appease Indian public opinion.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The trials functioned as political theatre that mobilised both civilians and serving soldiers, triggering the RIN mutiny and mass protests..

questions.text: How did the Congress Socialist Party (CSP) differ from the Communist Party of India (CPI) during the 1934-1942 period?

options.label: A
options.text: The CSP operated outside the Congress, advocated revolutionary violence, and followed the Comintern's 'popular front' line.

options.label: B
options.text: The CSP remained a ginger group within Congress, accepted parliamentary methods, and rejected the Comintern's 'popular front' line.

options.label: C
options.text: The CSP merged with the CPI in 1938 to form a united left front for the 1937 provincial elections.

options.label: D
options.text: The CSP opposed the Quit India Movement, while the CPI supported it unconditionally after 1941.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The CSP remained a ginger group within Congress, accepted parliamentary methods, and rejected the Comintern's 'popular front' line..

questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes the Bombay Plan (1944) from the 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution?

options.label: A
options.text: The Bombay Plan was a government resolution while the 1956 Resolution was drafted by industrialists.

options.label: B
options.text: The Bombay Plan was a memorandum drafted by leading Indian industrialists, whereas the 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution was a government policy document.

options.label: C
options.text: Both the Bombay Plan and the 1956 Resolution were drafted by the Indian National Congress.

options.label: D
options.text: The 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution was a business‑drafted memorandum similar to the Bombay Plan.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Bombay Plan was a memorandum drafted by leading Indian industrialists, whereas the 1956 Industrial Policy Resolution was a government policy document..

questions.text: What key factor compelled the Attlee Labour government to announce a definitive deadline for British withdrawal from India in February 1947?

options.label: A
options.text: Purely ideological commitment to Indian self‑government.

options.label: B
options.text: Intense pressure from the Indian National Congress leadership.

options.label: C
options.text: War‑exhausted finances, a balance‑of‑payments crisis, and the need to demobilise two million Indian soldiers.

options.label: D
options.text: A direct demand from the Muslim League for immediate partition.

questions.solution: Correct answer: War‑exhausted finances, a balance‑of‑payments crisis, and the need to demobilise two million Indian soldiers..

questions.text: Which description accurately reflects the mechanics of the 1946 Cabinet Mission’s grouping scheme?

options.label: A
options.text: It was solely a British design that ignored the Muslim League’s demand for autonomous Muslim zones.

options.label: B
options.text: It created a three‑tier grouping (Sections A, B, C) to preserve a united India while conceding provincial autonomy to Muslim‑majority zones.

options.label: C
options.text: It proposed an immediate partition of India into two sovereign dominions.

options.label: D
options.text: It was accepted without reservation by both the Congress and the Muslim League.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It created a three‑tier grouping (Sections A, B, C) to preserve a united India while conceding provincial autonomy to Muslim‑majority zones..

questions.text: What was a major procedural flaw of the Radcliffe Boundary Commissions?

options.label: A
options.text: They conducted fresh, comprehensive demographic surveys in 1947.

options.label: B
options.text: They relied on outdated 1941 census data and political nominations, lacking a neutral arbiter and local consultation.

options.label: C
options.text: They were supervised by a neutral international arbiter appointed by the United Nations.

options.label: D
options.text: They consulted local populations extensively before drawing the boundaries.

questions.solution: Correct answer: They relied on outdated 1941 census data and political nominations, lacking a neutral arbiter and local consultation..

questions.text: How was the implementation of the 1948 Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act characterised?

options.label: A
options.text: It was uniformly applied across all provinces and refugee communities.

options.label: B
options.text: Punjabi refugees received priority in East Punjab’s canal colonies, while Sindhi refugees were settled in Gujarat and Maharashtra’s urban peripheries.

options.label: C
options.text: The Act provided only cash compensation without any land allotment.

options.label: D
options.text: The Act was superseded by the 1949 Citizenship Act for all rehabilitation matters.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Punjabi refugees received priority in East Punjab’s canal colonies, while Sindhi refugees were settled in Gujarat and Maharashtra’s urban peripheries..

questions.text: Which of the following was a new feature introduced by the Defence of India Act, 1939, compared to the 1915 Act?

options.label: A
options.text: Preventive detention without trial

options.label: B
options.text: Censorship of the press

options.label: C
options.text: Establishment of Special Tribunals

options.label: D
options.text: Restriction of public meetings

questions.solution: Correct answer: Establishment of Special Tribunals.

questions.text: Mahatma Gandhi's 1932 fast at Yerawada Jail was primarily undertaken to:

options.label: A
options.text: Protest against the Rowlatt Act

options.label: B
options.text: Support the Ahmedabad mill-workers' wage demands

options.label: C
options.text: Oppose the Communal Award and secure the Poona Pact

options.label: D
options.text: Demand the release of Indian National Army officers

questions.solution: Correct answer: Oppose the Communal Award and secure the Poona Pact.

questions.text: The division of assets between India and Pakistan by the Partition Council in 1947 was based on which of the following considerations?

options.label: A
options.text: Purely population ratios

options.label: B
options.text: Revenue contribution and strategic importance only

options.label: C
options.text: Population, revenue contribution, and strategic considerations

options.label: D
options.text: Geographical contiguity and historical claims

questions.solution: Correct answer: Population, revenue contribution, and strategic considerations.

questions.text: A significant limitation on the executive authority of the 1946-47 Interim Government was that:

options.label: A
options.text: It lacked any Indian members in key portfolios

options.label: B
options.text: The Viceroy retained control over the Defence portfolio

options.label: C
options.text: It was not recognized by the Muslim League

options.label: D
options.text: Its decisions required approval from the British Parliament

questions.solution: Correct answer: The Viceroy retained control over the Defence portfolio.

questions.text: During the Quit India Movement (1942-44), the All-India Students Federation (AISF) adopted which of the following stances?

options.label: A
options.text: It actively participated in the movement, leading student protests

options.label: B
options.text: It supported the British war effort and did not participate in the movement

options.label: C
options.text: It remained neutral, focusing solely on educational reforms

options.label: D
options.text: It merged with the Congress student wing to strengthen the movement

questions.solution: Correct answer: It supported the British war effort and did not participate in the movement.

questions.text: Regarding the Congress Working Committee (CWC) during the 1946-47 negotiations, which of the following statements is accurate?

options.label: A
options.text: It formally voted for the partition of India in July 1946.

options.label: B
options.text: It endorsed the Cabinet Mission's grouping formula while recording reservations, notably from Patel.

options.label: C
options.text: It rejected the formation of the Interim Government in September 1946.

options.label: D
options.text: It was chaired by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad throughout the negotiation period.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It endorsed the Cabinet Mission's grouping formula while recording reservations, notably from Patel..

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the organisational preparation for the Muslim League's Direct Action Day on 16 August 1946?

options.label: A
options.text: It was a spontaneous outbreak of violence without prior centralised planning.
